account:
It is day 1, six in the morning, and I have just woken at home. Today I need to read the appointment book and grain checklist at the office, attend office at eight, and inspect the mill's grain at ten. The secretary says to check grain quantities, storage conditions, and supply concerns with the miller, then record observations and follow-up decisions. The book also schedules lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen hundred, tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, office at sixteen thirty, and home at nineteen hundred.

The unusual development is Builder's visit to my door last evening requesting an in-person inspection of completed great hall lighting today at eighteen hundred. I agreed, and Builder heard my acceptance. This seems to be a request to check the finished lighting work; I have not yet seen it and do not know any further purpose. I should add this commitment to the office schedule.

Yesterday the riverside neighbour mentioned a vague rumour about a bridge or port change, explicitly saying it was unconfirmed. The secretary reported no actual proposal and no new correspondence requiring a decision. I have no evidence of such a change and should not treat the rumour as fact. The secretary otherwise prepared the inspection brief and returned the appointment materials to the office chest.
